Name: DLG_C0_Opening_01
title: What Happened
speaker: NARRATOR
text: Eight months ago, under Saltmere Island, Vigor Biotech tested a virus they called V-7.

Name: DLG_C0_Opening_02
title: What Happened
speaker: NARRATOR
text: It was meant to make weak bodies strong. Old men. Sick men. People nobody would miss.

Name: DLG_C0_Opening_03
title: What Happened
speaker: NARRATOR
text: Subject seven was a dying fisherman. He did not stay dying.

Name: DLG_C0_Opening_04
title: What Happened
speaker: NARRATOR
text: Two of the staff were dead by morning. Vigor sealed the Annex and called it a flood.

Name: DLG_C0_Opening_05
title: What Happened
speaker: NARRATOR
text: What was left of the stock went into a container. The label said Medical Supplies.

Name: DLG_C0_Opening_06
title: What Happened
speaker: NARRATOR
text: Last night it came through Port Halvern. At 02:14, two dock workers opened it.

Name: DLG_C0_Opening_07
title: What Happened
speaker: NARRATOR
text: A cold mist came out. Breathe it, and it only takes the weak.

Name: DLG_C0_Opening_08
title: What Happened
speaker: NARRATOR
text: A bite takes anyone. And the strong come back stronger.

Name: DLG_C0_Opening_09
title: What Happened
speaker: NARRATOR
text: By dawn the port was gone. By breakfast it was walking into the city.

Name: DLG_C0_Opening_10
title: What Happened
speaker: LEON
text: None of that was on the news when I checked in.

Name: DLG_C0_CheckIn_01
title: Check-In
speaker: RUTH
text: Late one.

Name: DLG_C0_CheckIn_02
title: Check-In
speaker: LEON
text: Late flight. Cater, one night.

Name: DLG_C0_CheckIn_03
title: Check-In
speaker: RUTH
text: Three-oh-four. Elevator's out. Stairs are past the bar.

Name: DLG_C0_CheckIn_04
title: Check-In
speaker: LEON
text: Of course they are.

Name: DLG_C0_CheckIn_05
title: Check-In
speaker: RUTH
text: Breakfast is seven till ten.

Name: DLG_C0_CheckIn_06
title: Check-In
speaker: LEON
text: I'll be gone by seven.

Name: NAR_C0_KeySleeve
title: Key Card Sleeve
speaker: Gullwing Hotel
text:
GULLWING HOTEL · HARBOR AVENUE · MARROW BAY
Room 304

Breakfast 07:00 to 10:00 in the Harbor Room.
The elevator is out of service. We apologise for the climb.

On the back, in biro: "Ice machine on 2 works. 3 doesn't. — R."

Name: NAR_C0_Voicemail
title: Voicemail, 22:51
speaker: Lena Ortiz
text:
"Cater, it's Ortiz, field office. Pruitt wants you at the nine o'clock. Don't be late, he counts.

[A pause, traffic behind her.]

And don't eat at the Gullwing. I've seen the kitchen. See you at nine."

Name: NAR_C0_TVBulletin
title: Morning Bulletin
speaker: Channel 6
text:
[The TV wakes on its own at 07:00, an alarm somebody set and forgot.]

EMERGENCY BROADCAST — HARBOR DISTRICT
Residents between Harbor Avenue and the port are advised to remain indoors. Do not approach persons who appear unwell. Do not attempt to restrain them.

[The anchor is reading it off paper. Her hands are shaking. The ticker under her still runs the weather.]

Name: DLG_C0_Window_01
title: The Window
speaker: LEON
text: That's not drunk.

Name: DLG_C0_Door_01
title: The Knock
speaker: ORTIZ
text: Cater. Cater, it's Ortiz.

Name: DLG_C0_Door_02
title: The Knock
speaker: LEON
text: You knock like one of them.

Name: DLG_C0_Door_03
title: The Knock
speaker: ORTIZ
text: You answer the door like one. Put the bottle down.

Name: DLG_C0_Door_04
title: The Knock
speaker: ORTIZ
text: You didn't pick up. Pruitt sent me. The port went dark at three and it's spreading this way.

Name: DLG_C0_Door_05
title: The Knock
speaker: LEON
text: What is it?

Name: DLG_C0_Door_06
title: The Knock
speaker: ORTIZ
text: Something off a Vigor container. Nobody's saying more than that on an open line.

Name: DLG_C0_Door_07
title: The Knock
speaker: ORTIZ
text: Your sidearm. Thirty rounds. That's all I could carry.

Name: DLG_C0_Door_08
title: The Knock
speaker: ORTIZ
text: And the knife. Quieter.

Name: DLG_C0_Door_09
title: The Knock
speaker: LEON
text: They come for noise?

Name: DLG_C0_Door_10
title: The Knock
speaker: ORTIZ
text: They wander toward it. They only come for you if they see you.

Name: DLG_C0_Door_11
title: The Knock
speaker: ORTIZ
text: Break their line of sight and wait. They lose you. Whatever's in them chews up the part that remembers.

Name: DLG_C0_Door_12
title: The Knock
speaker: ORTIZ
text: Bureau car, garage level two, bay fourteen. Key's yours. You drive, I shoot.

Name: DLG_C0_Stairwell_01
title: The Stairwell
speaker: ORTIZ
text: Too many. Go down, I'll pull them up.

Name: DLG_C0_Stairwell_02
title: The Stairwell
speaker: LEON
text: Ortiz —

Name: DLG_C0_Stairwell_03
title: The Stairwell
speaker: ORTIZ
text: Bay fourteen. Don't make me wait.

Name: NAR_C0_NightLog
title: Night Desk Log
speaker: Ruth
text:
23:10. Cater, 304. Polite. Tired.

02:40. Ambulances on Harbor Ave. Lots.

03:55. Man from 309 says someone is trying his door. Told him it's the wind.

04:30. Phone lines busy. All of them.

05:10. A man came in off the street holding his arm. I put him in the back office with the first aid kit. He's quiet now. I'll check on him in a minute.

Name: NAR_C0_UnderDoor
title: Note Under Door 309
text:
Folded hotel stationery, pushed halfway under the door from the inside:

DON'T OPEN FOR HIM.
HE SOUNDS LIKE FRANK.
HE ISN'T.

Name: NAR_C0_GarageSign
title: Garage Notice
speaker: Gullwing Hotel
text:
GUEST PARKING — LEVEL P2
Bays 1–20. Reserved: bays 12–16, Federal pool vehicles.

The ramp gate opens automatically for vehicles leaving. Please drive slowly. Pedestrians have right of way.

Name: DLG_C0_Car_01
title: Bay Fourteen
speaker: ORTIZ
text: Drive.

Name: DLG_C0_Car_02
title: Bay Fourteen
speaker: LEON
text: You took your time.

Name: DLG_C0_Car_03
title: Bay Fourteen
speaker: ORTIZ
text: I took the long way. Kestrel Street, the field office. Don't stop for anyone.

Name: DLG_C0_Drive_01
title: The Drive
speaker: ORTIZ
text: Right out of the ramp. Stay off the pavement, they come out of the doorways.

Name: DLG_C0_Drive_02
title: The Drive
speaker: ORTIZ
text: Bus across the lane. Go round on the left.

Name: DLG_C0_Drive_03
title: The Drive
speaker: ORTIZ
text: Runners. Don't slow down. Slowing down is how they get on the car.

Name: DLG_C0_Drive_04
title: The Drive
speaker: LEON
text: They're fast.

Name: DLG_C0_Drive_05
title: The Drive
speaker: ORTIZ
text: The big ones are. The old ones can barely stand.

Name: DLG_C0_Drive_06
title: The Drive
speaker: ORTIZ
text: Left at the lights. There aren't any lights. Left anyway.

Name: DLG_C0_Drive_07
title: The Drive
speaker: ORTIZ
text: Kestrel Street. The gate with the sandbags. That's us.

Name: DLG_C0_HQ_01
title: The Field Office
speaker: PRUITT
text: Cater. You're late.

Name: DLG_C0_HQ_02
title: The Field Office
speaker: LEON
text: Traffic.

Name: DLG_C0_HQ_03
title: The Field Office
speaker: PRUITT
text: Port Halvern went dark at three. Vigor container. I'm taking the team in at noon.

Name: DLG_C0_HQ_04
title: The Field Office
speaker: LEON
text: I'm coming.

Name: DLG_C0_HQ_05
title: The Field Office
speaker: PRUITT
text: You're a liaison. You hold the phones. If we don't call by dark, you call the cavalry.

Name: DLG_C0_HQ_06
title: The Field Office
speaker: ORTIZ
text: We'll be back by dark, Cater. Keep the coffee on.

Name: DLG_C0_Cards_01
title: After the Briefing
speaker: NARRATOR
text: 13:00. Pruitt, Ortiz and Whitlock land at Port Halvern.

Name: DLG_C0_Cards_02
title: After the Briefing
speaker: NARRATOR
text: 17:40. Pruitt's last call: "Port police are here. Hale's people." Then nothing.

Name: DLG_C0_Cards_03
title: After the Briefing
speaker: NARRATOR
text: 22:00. Nobody answers the cavalry either. Leon hires a boat.

Name: NAR_C1_ManifestA
title: Inbound Manifest — Berth 2, Yard C
speaker: Priya Dann
text:
INBOUND MANIFEST / PORT HALVERN / BERTH 2 -> YARD C
Vessel: MV Coldwater Rose. Discharged 23:50.

Unit VGR-7718. Consignor: VIGOR BIOTECH LOGISTICS. Contents declared: MEDICAL SUPPLIES, NON-HAZ.
Temp log: -4 C maintained dockside. Reefer plug 14.
Customs: CLEARED ON PAPER. No physical inspection.
Handling note (consignor): DO NOT BREAK SEAL. DO NOT INSPECT. Consignor agent collects at 06:00.

Clerk's margin, in pen: Non-haz doesn't need minus four. Flagged it to Sully. Sully says sign it and go home.

Name: NAR_C1_ManifestB
title: Manifest Amendment 7718-A
text:
AMENDMENT TO MANIFEST VGR-7718
Filed 01:02. Filed by: terminal override, badge not recorded.

Storage reassigned: REEFER ROW -> YARD C, STACK 4, GROUND TIER.
Reason given: "consignor request, ground access".
Plug 14 released. Unit now UNPOWERED.

Second margin note, different hand: whoever moved it took it off the cold plug four hours before pickup. That's not access. That's so nobody walks past it.

Name: NAR_C1_ClerkDiary
title: Day Clerk's Desk Diary
speaker: Priya Dann
text:
Tuesday. Third Vigor unit this month. Same consignor, same wording, same nobody-opens-it. The lads have started calling them coffins. I asked them not to.

Wednesday. Bert's back on nights. He shouldn't be. He had the chest thing all winter and he still walks the whole fence line because he says the camera on Stack 4 is blind. He's seventy-one. Somebody should tell the office. I'm the office.

Thursday. Half the day shift didn't come in. Nobody's answering the harbour line. I'm writing this because I don't know what else to do with my hands.

Name: NAR_C1_EmailVigor
title: Email: Re: 7718 handling
speaker: Vigor Biotech Logistics
text:
FROM: logistics@vigorbiotech
TO: terminal.super@porthalvern
SUBJECT: Re: 7718 handling

Our handling instruction stands. The unit is not to be opened, sampled, photographed or scanned, by your staff or by customs.

Your clearance for this lane is already authorised at city level. If any officer raises it, give them the authorisation number and nothing else. Do not put the number in writing.

Our agent collects at 06:00. Keep the lane clear and keep your night crew off Stack 4.

Name: NAR_C1_EmailReply
title: Email: Re: Re: 7718 handling
speaker: Marcus Sully
text:
FROM: terminal.super@porthalvern
TO: logistics@vigorbiotech
SUBJECT: Re: Re: 7718 handling

Understood. Lane's clear.

For the record, I'd be happier if the paperwork matched the temperature. Minus four on a medical-supplies declaration gets questions from people I can't wave an authorisation number at.

I've moved night crew off Stack 4 on the rota. Varga's on Crane 3 and he does what he's told. Begg and Kelso are reefer row. Linnane walks the fence and he's half deaf, so that's fine.

Last one of these, Marcus.

Name: NAR_C1_PruittRadio
title: Crushed Field Radio
text:
A federal-issue handheld, flattened edge-on — something heavy came down on it at an angle. The channel wheel is snapped off at 4. The battery pack is still warm enough to have been live within the day.

Taped inside the cover, a strip of paper in blunt pencil: D. PRUITT / ORTIZ ch4 / WHITLOCK ch4 / IF SPLIT, REGROUP NORTH PIER.

Nobody regrouped. The drag marks going inland are two sets of heels, side by side, and nobody dragged themselves.

Name: NAR_C1_WatchRound
title: Watchman's Round Sheet
speaker: Bert Linnane
text:
FENCE ROUND — NIGHTS — INITIAL EACH POINT

01:00 gate / BL  01:30 reefer row / BL  02:00 stack 4 / BL
02:30 stack 4 / BL — mist on the ground here, cold, smells like a dentist
03:00 ______
03:30 ______

Under the empty lines, in a shaky hand that doesn't match the initials above: he's up. bert's up and he's not right. don't come down here. — T.B.

Name: NAR_C1_Tape0214
title: Security Camera Log — Yard C, Stack 4
text:
OVERNIGHT LOG / CAM 11 / YARD C STACK 4 / NO AUDIO

02:14 — Two men at a ground-tier unit, 7718. One works a bar under the seal. The door swings. White mist pours out low and stays low, the way cold does.

02:31 — An old man in a watchman's coat walks into frame through the mist, hand on his chest. He stops. He sits down against the container like a man who has decided to rest. He does not get up.

02:58 — One of the workers comes back with a flask. He kneels. The old man takes his wrist and bites through it. The worker gets clear and runs holding his arm.

03:40 — The same worker stands under the camera. He is not holding his arm any more. He takes the Stack 4 gate in both hands and pulls until the lock tears out of the frame. He is faster leaving than he was arriving.

Name: NAR_C1_PA_Loop
title: Warehouse PA — Looping Announcement
speaker: Port Halvern PA
text:
[A recorded woman's voice, cheerful, on a loop. It has been playing to an empty warehouse for twenty hours.]

"Attention Yard C. Due to an operational incident, all personnel are to muster at the north pier for head count. Do not use the yard gates. Do not approach Stack 4."

[Click. Hiss. Then a live voice cuts over it, close to the microphone, fast:]

"Nobody's at the pier. Whoever's listening, the pier is where they went and the pier is where it — "

[The loop resumes.]

Name: NAR_C1_OrtizBody
title: Agent Ortiz
text:
Federal ID in the vest pocket: ORTIZ, LENA R. Sidearm locked back on an empty magazine, slide forward on nothing. Fourteen casings inside two metres of where she sat down.

Two bites, left forearm and shoulder. The shoulder one was wrapped with her own cravat, neatly, one-handed.

She is still holding a notebook against her ribs. Her thumb has worn the cover through on one page, like she read it over and over while she waited.

She did not rise. Somebody made sure of that, and then walked away, and the casings say she was alone by then.

Name: NAR_C1_ShiftRota
title: Gantry Shift Rota Board
speaker: Marcus Sully
text:
GANTRY CRANE ROTA — WEEK 41 — DON'T SWAP WITHOUT ASKING ME

CRANE 1 — DAY (06:00-14:00) — ABEL
CRANE 2 — SWING (14:00-22:00) — SULLY
CRANE 3 — NIGHT (22:00-06:00) — DMITRI

START-UP ORDER, EVERY TIME: bring up whoever's on shift now, then the next shift round the clock, then the last. The main breaker will not carry three cold motors in the wrong order. It trips, it bangs, and I am not walking out there at three in the morning again.

Taped under the board: fuse lives in the cabinet in here, NOT in the control house, because the control house floods.

Name: NAR_C1_VargaLog
title: Crane 3 Cab Recorder — Night Shift
speaker: Dmitri Varga
text:
[Cab recorder, rain on glass, motor hum.]

02:16. Something's venting at Stack 4. Begg's down there with a bar. Told him over the tannoy to leave it. He waved.

03:05. Bert's on the ground and Kelso's screaming. I'm not coming down. I've got forty metres of air under me and a locked hatch and that is the most sensible place in this port.

04:50. It's in the cab stair. I've got the hook block hard against the hatch. Hand's bad. Something got the hand.

[Long pause. Breathing changes pitch.]

05:30. If somebody plays this. I keep the hook with me. Tell my mother I kept — [recording ends]

Name: NAR_C1_KelsoSlip
title: Overtime Slip
speaker: Dan Kelso
text:
OVERTIME AUTHORISATION — NIGHTS — 4 HRS
NAME: D. KELSO  BADGE: 2209
REASON: "consignor assist, reefer row"

On the back, in biro: Tom says the Vigor one's worth a look. Says the last three had cold boxes in them and nobody counted the cold boxes. I said no. He asked twice. It's four hours' money and Bert's the only one on the fence and Bert can't hear a thing.

I'm going to regret this at six in the morning.

Name: NAR_C1_PruittScratch
title: Scratched Into the Cage Frame
speaker: Dale Pruitt
text:
Gouged into the paint beside the keypad with a knife point, fast and deep:

CAGE = WHEN IT OPENED

Under it, smaller: GEAR INSIDE. ORTIZ IS IN THE WAREHOUSE. I'M GOING TO THE OFFICE TO CALL IT IN.
Under that, scratched shallower, like he came back once: PORT POLICE ARE HERE. WRONG ONES.

Name: NAR_C1_CustomsSlip
title: Customs Inspection Slip (Void)
text:
PHYSICAL INSPECTION REQUEST — UNIT VGR-7718
Raised by: night customs officer, badge 41
Ground: declaration inconsistent with carriage temperature.

Stamped diagonally across the form in red: WITHDRAWN — CITY AUTHORISATION ON FILE.

Badge 41 wrote one line at the bottom before he filed it anyway: Authorisation came from a police number, not a customs number. I've kept a copy where the keypad is, because the keypad code is a date only four of us know, and after tonight I'd like somebody to come looking.

Name: NAR_C1_OrtizNotes
title: Ortiz — Field Notes
speaker: Lena Ortiz
text:
13:00. Landed. Port's quiet in the wrong way — gear left running, nobody on it.

14:20. Dock office CCTV holds an overnight log. Pruitt watched four minutes of it and went grey. He locked our case in the customs cage and set the code to the timestamp. He said if anyone federal comes after us, they'll read the tape before they find the cage, and then they'll already know the number.

16:00. Whitlock's chasing the consignor name. Vigor Biotech. Everything here routes through a city authorisation nobody will put in writing.

17:40. Pruitt's on the radio to Bay Central. He's saying "port police". He's saying "Hale's people". Then he isn't saying anything.

Later. My arm's wrapped. I can hear them walking the aisles. Whoever reads this: the tape is the whole case. Take the tape.

Cater, if it's you: I said we'd be back by dark. Sorry about the coffee.

Name: NAR_C1_SuppressantLabel
title: V-7 Suppressant — Auto-injector Label
speaker: Vigor Biotech
text:
V-7 SUPPRESSANT / AUTO-INJECTOR / SINGLE USE
FOR AUTHORISED FIELD PERSONNEL. NOT FOR SALE. NOT A CURE.

Administer to outer thigh within 30 minutes of exposure or bite. Resets serum titre to baseline. Does NOT clear the agent from tissue. Repeat exposure requires repeat dose.

Side panel, printed small: Suppression is not remission. Personnel reporting more than two doses are to be reassigned and are not to be told why.

Name: NAR_C1_BreakerNote
title: Taped Above the Breaker
speaker: Marcus Sully
text:
IF THE MAIN TRIPS:
1. Don't just slam it back in. Let it sit thirty seconds or you'll weld the contacts.
2. It bangs like a gunshot and every gull in the estuary lifts. Expect company — last month it brought the whole night crew out of the break room wanting to know who died.
3. Then do it again IN ORDER. On shift first. Round the clock from there.

Three tries and I'm calling the contractor and it's coming out of somebody's hours.

Name: NAR_C1_FusePlate
title: Panel Plate — Gantry Supply
text:
GANTRY SUPPLY — 400A CARTRIDGE FUSE — SLOT EMPTY

Stencilled on the empty carrier, factory lettering: DO NOT ENERGISE GANTRY BUS WITHOUT CARTRIDGE IN PLACE.

A strip of gaffer tape over it, hand-marked: spare cartridge is in the break room cabinet. Control house takes water over the sill on a spring tide and I'm not drowning four hundred quid of fuse.

Below the three gantry switches, a brass plate: C1 / C2 / C3. The yard gate motor and the yard crane are on the same bus. No power, no gate.

Name: NAR_C1_KelsoGate
title: Stack 4 Gate
text:
The personnel gate into Stack 4 is standing open because the lock plate is gone. Not cut, not drilled — torn out, taking a fist of chain-link and three rivets with it. The steel is bowed outward where two hands held it.

A Vigor-issue high-visibility vest is snagged on the burr, size XL, badge 2209 on the chest tab.

Whoever did this was strong before. He got stronger after.

Name: NAR_C1_DropZoneSign
title: Yard Safety Sign
text:
DANGER — SUSPENDED LOAD ZONE — KEEP OUT WHEN STRIPES ARE LIT

Ground marking: yellow and black hazard stripes, four metres square, directly beneath the yard crane's hook block.

RELEASE LEVER AT CRANE LEG. The lever drops whatever is on the hook. It does not ask twice and it does not stop halfway.

Spray-painted underneath by somebody with no respect for signage: two cans per shift. then you're hanging nothing and you're on your own.

Name: NAR_C1_ContainerSeal
title: Broken Seal — VGR-7718
text:
A bolt seal, levered rather than cut, still hanging from the locking bar by its sheared stem. The barrel is stamped VIGOR BIOTECH and, beneath that, a lot number: V7-1140-SM.

SM. The same two letters are on every crate stencil inside the unit.

The pry bar is on the ground where it was dropped. There is frost on the door sill and nothing has been cold in this yard for twenty hours.

Name: NAR_C1_ContainerInterior
title: Inside VGR-7718
text:
Eleven foam-lined transit cases in racks. Ten are closed and intact. The eleventh is open, and its cradle is moulded for four cylinders. Three cylinders are still seated. The fourth cradle holds a cylinder with a split collar and a vent valve wound fully open.

Stencil on the rack end: ANNEX RECOVERY — SM — RETURN TO TOWER, DO NOT DECANT.

A clipboard chained to the wall: RECOVERED FROM SALTMERE ANNEX, SEALED STORE. Recovering technician signature is two letters and a long ragged line, as though his hand was shaking. O. Q.

Name: NAR_C1_VargaNote
title: Pinned Inside the Crane Shed
speaker: Dmitri Varga
text:
Pinned to the shed board with a shackle pin, written on the back of a load chart:

I am not sick. I am cold all the time and my arm is growing and I can feel the chain in it, which is a stupid thing to write and it is true.

I stay in the shed. If I stay in the shed I only hurt the ones that come in.

If you are reading this you came in.

Don't stand on the stripes.

Name: NAR_C1_NightCrewPhoto
title: Night Crew, Week 39
text:
A phone photo printed on office paper and pinned over the break room kettle. Five people crowded under a gantry leg in rain, all grinning, all holding mugs.

Names biroed on the white border, left to right: ABEL — SULLY — BERT (71 AND STILL ON NIGHTS, DISGRACE) — TOM — DAN.

At the edge of frame, half out of it, a tall man in a crane harness who did not want to be in the picture. Somebody has written DMITRI and an arrow.

In the corner, a date three weeks before tonight.

Name: NAR_C1_BeggPhone
title: Phone on the Reefer Row Steps
speaker: Tom Begg
text:
A work phone, cracked, 4% battery, one unsent message open on screen.

To: DAN K
02:51 — mate come back the old boy is on the deck by 7718 he aint breathing right
02:53 — DAN
02:53 — dan he got up
03:02 — dont come back
03:04 — i can hear you in the row. dont answer me if its you. if its you dont answer me

The message was never sent. There is no signal in reefer row and there never has been.

Name: NAR_C1_HarbourBoard
title: Harbour Notice Board
speaker: Halvern Harbour Authority
text:
NOTICE TO MARINERS — RIVER MOUTH

Saltmere Point: harbour radio station manned 24h, channel 16 and port band. Ferry service to Saltmere SUSPENDED until further notice — no crew available.

Tender berth: south boat dock, inside the cargo shutter. Shutter is keyed. Key held by yard supervisor or duty gantry operator ONLY.

Tide tonight: high water 23:55. The boat dock floods ankle-deep at the top of the tide. Watch the water. Things wash in on a high tide and they don't always wash out.

Name: RAD_C1_MaraFirst_01
title: First Contact
speaker: MARA
text: Port channel, anyone. This is Halvern Harbor Radio. Please.

Name: RAD_C1_MaraFirst_02
title: First Contact
speaker: LEON
text: Agent Cater, federal. I'm on the north pier.

Name: RAD_C1_MaraFirst_03
title: First Contact
speaker: MARA
text: Federal. The last ones stopped answering.

Name: RAD_C1_MaraFirst_04
title: First Contact
speaker: LEON
text: That's why I'm here.

Name: RAD_C1_MaraFirst_05
title: First Contact
speaker: MARA
text: I'm Mara. I'm across the river on Saltmere. I can see your flashlight.

Name: RAD_C1_MaraFirst_06
title: First Contact
speaker: LEON
text: Then you know I'm alone. Talk me through it.

Name: RAD_C1_PruittRadio_01
title: The Crushed Radio
speaker: LEON
text: Found a federal handset. Someone stood on it.

Name: RAD_C1_PruittRadio_02
title: The Crushed Radio
speaker: MARA
text: There were three of them. I heard one shouting yesterday evening, then nothing on any band.

Name: RAD_C1_PruittRadio_03
title: The Crushed Radio
speaker: LEON
text: Blood goes inland. I'll follow it while it's still wet.

Name: RAD_C1_SafeRoom_01
title: The Dock Office
speaker: MARA
text: The dock office has a relay set. Key it and I'll log you in — that way I know you're still there.

Name: RAD_C1_SafeRoom_02
title: The Dock Office
speaker: LEON
text: Understood. There's a stack of manifests on this desk with a company name all over them.

Name: RAD_C1_SafeRoom_03
title: The Dock Office
speaker: MARA
text: Read it to me later. There's a monitor in there too. The night log runs on it.

Name: RAD_C1_AfterTape_01
title: After the Tape
speaker: LEON
text: Old man went first. The big one went faster.

Name: RAD_C1_AfterTape_02
title: After the Tape
speaker: MARA
text: Owen said not to open anything.

Name: RAD_C1_AfterTape_03
title: After the Tape
speaker: MARA
text: Never mind.

Name: RAD_C1_AfterTape_04
title: After the Tape
speaker: LEON
text: Timestamp was 02:14. I'll keep that one.

Name: RAD_C1_Warehouse_01
title: Warehouse 3
speaker: MARA
text: Warehouse 3 is your only way to the yard side. It's a long room full of pallets.

Name: RAD_C1_Warehouse_02
title: Warehouse 3
speaker: LEON
text: Three of them on the floor. They haven't looked up yet.

Name: RAD_C1_Warehouse_03
title: Warehouse 3
speaker: MARA
text: Then don't let them see you. Throw something and they'll wander to the noise. They only come for what they can see.

Name: RAD_C1_Warehouse_04
title: Warehouse 3
speaker: LEON
text: Walking past is cheaper than shooting. Noted.

Name: RAD_C1_Ortiz_01
title: Ortiz
speaker: LEON
text: It's Ortiz. She said they'd be back by dark.

Name: RAD_C1_Ortiz_02
title: Ortiz
speaker: MARA
text: I'm sorry.

Name: RAD_C1_Ortiz_03
title: Ortiz
speaker: LEON
text: She left notes. She was better at this than whoever sent her.

Name: RAD_C1_Reborn_01
title: The First Reborn
speaker: LEON
text: It got back up. It is not the same shape it was.

Name: RAD_C1_Reborn_02
title: The First Reborn
speaker: MARA
text: They do that if you leave them halfway. Bert's lot went quiet and then they didn't.

Name: RAD_C1_Reborn_03
title: The First Reborn
speaker: MARA
text: Head, or fire, or your knife on the ground. Finish them or they finish standing up.

Name: RAD_C1_Reborn_04
title: The First Reborn
speaker: LEON
text: Then nobody gets left halfway.

Name: RAD_C1_HintCage_01
title: Hint — Customs Cage
speaker: MARA
text: A customs cage is where they put the things they don't want walking off. Four digits, so it's a date or a time to somebody.

Name: RAD_C1_HintCage_02
title: Hint — Customs Cage
speaker: MARA
text: There's writing scratched by the keypad. Whoever set the code left you the sentence, not the number.

Name: RAD_C1_HintCage_03
title: Hint — Customs Cage
speaker: MARA
text: When it opened. You watched it open. Put the time on the keypad — zero two one four.

Name: RAD_C1_HintCrane_01
title: Hint — Crane Power
speaker: MARA
text: Dead panel means a pulled fuse. Nobody keeps a spare in a shed that floods — try where they make tea.

Name: RAD_C1_HintCrane_02
title: Hint — Crane Power
speaker: MARA
text: Three switches, three cranes, and a supervisor who wrote the start-up order on the rota board. Whoever's on shift comes up first.

Name: RAD_C1_HintCrane_03
title: Hint — Crane Power
speaker: MARA
text: It's the middle of the night, Cater. Nights is Crane 3. Then round the clock — day, then swing. Three, one, two.

Name: RAD_C1_Kelso_01
title: The Big One
speaker: LEON
text: The one from the tape is out here. He took a shotgun shell and kept coming.

Name: RAD_C1_Kelso_02
title: The Big One
speaker: MARA
text: The bitten ones come back stronger than they were alive. The sick ones you can walk away from. Not him.

Name: RAD_C1_HintHookman_01
title: Hint — The Hookman
speaker: MARA
text: Don't trade with him. He's got twelve feet of reach and you've got a handgun.

Name: RAD_C1_HintHookman_02
title: Hint — The Hookman
speaker: MARA
text: He throws that hook and when it bites steel instead of you, he can't let go. Watch his back when he's pulling.

Name: RAD_C1_HintHookman_03
title: Hint — The Hookman
speaker: MARA
text: There's a container hanging over those painted stripes and a lever at the crane leg. Get him on the stripes and pull it.

Name: RAD_C1_Shutter_01
title: The Shutter
speaker: LEON
text: He was carrying the shutter key on the chain. He never used it.

Name: RAD_C1_Shutter_02
title: The Shutter
speaker: MARA
text: He locked himself in with them. Through that shutter there's a tender berth. Get in it.

Name: DLG_C1_Arrival_01
title: Arrival
speaker: HANK
text: This is as close as I go.

Name: DLG_C1_Arrival_02
title: Arrival
speaker: LEON
text: Pruitt's team came in here?

Name: DLG_C1_Arrival_03
title: Arrival
speaker: HANK
text: Around noon. Nobody's called since.

Name: DLG_C1_Arrival_04
title: Arrival
speaker: LEON
text: Then somebody should.

Name: DLG_C1_Departure_01
title: Boat Departure
speaker: MARA
text: Saltmere's the lights across the river. I'm on the point, in the radio station.

Name: DLG_C1_Departure_02
title: Boat Departure
speaker: LEON
text: Keep the lights on.

Name: DLG_C1_Departure_03
title: Boat Departure
speaker: MARA
text: They're all I've got.

Name: NAR_C2_TideWarning
title: Parish Notice: High Water
speaker: Saltmere Parish Council
text:
POSTED 11 DAYS AGO.
The pumps at the sluice are off until the county sends a part. Expect water to the first step on Quay Row and the whole of Chapel Lane.
Do not wade. Two people have gone in this month and one did not come out.
If you cannot get to the ferry, stay upstairs, keep a light in the window, and we will come door to door.
We did not come door to door. There was nobody left to send. - R. Teague, warden (added by hand)

Name: NAR_C2_MarketWall
title: Scrawl on the Market Tiles
text:
Written in gutting-table chalk, three feet high, across the white tiles:
DON'T DRINK THE WATER
DON'T BOIL IT EITHER
IT CAME UP THE DRAINS FROM UNDER US
Below it, smaller, in a different hand: Nan drank it and she's fine. She's 80. She's fine.
Below that, in the first hand again: she is not fine.

Name: NAR_C2_CalderDiary3
title: Calder's Pages, 1 of 5
speaker: Dr. Ines Calder
text:
Taped under the auctioneer's desk, market hall.
I am splitting this up. If one place burns or floods, the rest keeps.
Start here, because this is where I understood it. I bought a crab off a man on this floor who could not lift his own box. Eight months later I read his file. He was the first one we put it in, and he lifted a steel door off its runners.
Elias calls that a result. I called it a man who used to sell me crab.
The other pages are where I pray and where I sleep.

Name: NAR_C2_IceReceipt
title: Cold Store Receipt Book
speaker: Saltmere Fish Market
text:
Carbon copy, third sheet from the back.
ACCOUNT: VIGOR BIOTECH (SITE SERVICES), 14 months standing.
ITEM: Cold store bay 3, exclusive hire. Flake ice, 400 kg weekly. Transport crates, returned empty.
NOTE FROM THE CLERK: they pay six months up front and they never take fish. Bay 3 is theirs and we don't go in it. The crates go down the shore road at night, not to the ferry.
PAID. Stamped. Signed for by a driver who printed VIGOR in the name box and nothing else.

Name: NAR_C2_MarketShiftNote
title: Cold Store Door Note
speaker: Pell
text:
Nailed inside the roller door of bay 3.
TOM - the lighthouse crank is on the nail in here, not in the hut. The keeper brought it down to lever the ice chute in March and never carried it back up, and now he's not answering his door either.
If anybody from the county asks, the crank is at the lighthouse where it belongs.
If anybody from VIGOR asks, you've never seen a crank.
- Pell

Name: NAR_C2_FamilyNote
title: Note on a Wardrobe Door
speaker: Jess Arrow
text:
Pinned at child height on the inside of the wardrobe.
BABS - if you are reading this in here then you did the right thing and I am proud of you.
Count to two hundred. Slow. They go away when the water is still.
Do not open it for the noise. The noise is not me. I will knock three times and say your whole name, both names, and if I don't say both names it isn't me.
Mum.

Name: NAR_C2_PhotoVossHale
title: Water-Stained Photograph
text:
A framed photo on a shelf of medical journals, the bottom third bloomed and buckled by damp.
A marquee, a long table, a cut ribbon. Two men shaking hands over it and holding the pose a beat too long for the camera.
On the left, younger, in a good coat: Dr. Elias Voss.
On the right, in dress uniform with the braid: Chief Warren Hale, Marrow Bay Police.
The banner behind them is legible where the water stopped: VIGOR BIOTECH - SALTMERE SITE - COMMUNITY PARTNERS.
On the back, in Calder's hand: they have known each other for eleven years. I keep forgetting that, so here it is on a wall.

Name: NAR_C2_VossLetter
title: Printed Email: Re: your resignation
speaker: Dr. Elias Voss
text:
FROM: E. Voss
TO: I. Calder
SUBJECT: Re: your resignation

Iness,

You keep using the word accident. An accident is a thing you do not repeat. I have repeated it nine times.

You met Penhallow. You shook a dying man's hand. Two months later that hand could bend rebar. You want me to call that a tragedy because the man it happened to did not stay polite.

The resignation is not accepted, because there is nothing to resign from. There is no programme. There is a sealed building under an island and a contract that says I may keep it sealed.

Come back before someone decides you are a loose end. I would rather it were me who said that to you than someone with a different job.

E.

Name: NAR_C2_CalderDiary4
title: Calder's Pages, 2 of 5
speaker: Dr. Ines Calder
text:
Oilcloth packet, cellar shelf, behind the preserve jars.
The hymn sheet is folded in with this page on purpose. I am not musical and I never was, so if you have found both, you are looking for the same thing I hid.
I put the bell tower key inside the organ. The verger showed me the panel behind the pipe shutter years ago, when he was proud of the thing. Play the verse and the shutter opens, the way it opens for the bell ringers.
Six notes. They are written on the sheet. Play them in the order they are written and nothing else, because that organ is loud and this town listens now.

Name: NAR_C2_HymnSheet
title: Hymn Sheet: "Low Tide"
speaker: Saltmere Chapel Hymnal
text:
A single sheet, foxed at the edges, hand-ruled.
HYMN 42 - LOW TIDE - verse 1, pedal line only (as played at Saltmere)

D    G    E    D    A    D
Down  go  every  dark  anchor  down

Under the stave, in pencil: six pedals, left to right as written. The organist's hand, not Calder's.
Under that, in Calder's hand: six. Not five. Not seven. The last one is a D again and everybody gets that wrong.

Name: NAR_C2_CalderDiary5
title: Calder's Pages, 3 of 5
speaker: Dr. Ines Calder
text:
Same packet, cellar.
I have written the important part nine times and burned it eight. Here it is plain.
It was never a weapon. Elias wanted a treatment. He wanted to take a body that was failing and give it back more than it lost, and the strain does exactly that, which is the whole problem. It only takes in the weak, and it gives them strength they never had, and it takes everything else.
He did not build a disease. He built a success, and the success is what you met in the street.
The work is not in the city. It is below the island. Under my feet while I write this.

Name: NAR_C2_AudioLog_Calder
title: Dictaphone, Tape Side B
speaker: Dr. Ines Calder
text:
(tape hiss, a chair, water moving somewhere below)
They turned the pumps off three days ago and told the council it was a part on order. It is not a part. The basin is meant to come up. When the basin comes up, the lower doors flood and nobody goes down the stair, and the sealed building stays sealed.
(pause)
I am going to the harbor tonight to look at the gate myself. If the wheel is off the capstan then I am right and somebody took it off, and if somebody took it off then they know I have been asking.
(a long breath)
If this is the last side of this tape, the pages are in three places and I am sorry about the organ. It really is very loud.

Name: NAR_C2_CalderDiary1
title: Calder's Pages, 4 of 5
speaker: Dr. Ines Calder
text:
Folded into hymnal 42 in the third pew, chapel nave.
Eight months ago I signed a consent form for a man who could not hold the pen. Trial seven. We called him Subject 7 because Elias says names make people sentimental, and he is right, they do.
He killed Aldous and he killed Ruth and he did it with his hands, and the report I typed says ADVERSE EVENT, EQUIPMENT.
I typed that. Nobody made me.
So I am not writing this to be forgiven. I am writing it so that the next person who comes through this chapel does not have to work it out from scratch.

Name: NAR_C2_CalderDiary2
title: Calder's Pages, 5 of 5
speaker: Dr. Ines Calder
text:
Inside the vestry hymn cupboard, chapel.
Two routes, and I want this written by someone who measured it.
Breathe it as mist or drink it out of a bad tap, and it only takes if your body is already losing. The old, the sick, the worn out. Everyone else coughs and goes to work.
But a bite is a full dose straight in, and a full dose does not care how strong you are. It cares very much afterwards. The stronger the body, the worse the thing that stands up in it.
So the ones to fear here are not the grandmothers. They are the harbor men.

Name: NAR_C2_VergerNote
title: Verger's Instructions, Pinned to the Organ Bench
speaker: Howell Teague, verger
text:
FOR WHOEVER PLAYS WHILE I AM IN HOSPITAL.
The pedal board is the only thing still true on this instrument. The manuals are swollen and two stops are dead, so play the pedal line only and the congregation will cope.
The shutter over the small pipes is on the same linkage as the bell tower latch. Play the opening of 42 correctly and it draws back. Play it wrong and you get the flat chord, which is the loudest sound in this parish, and then you may start again.
Pedals are lettered on the brass. Do not improvise. I will know.

Name: NAR_C2_HymnBoard
title: Hymn Board by the Chancel
text:
Slotted wooden numbers, three of the four still hanging.
THIS SUNDAY
18 - Bright Is The Morning
42 - LOW TIDE
7 - (number missing, slot empty)
EVENSONG CANCELLED - WATER
Chalked across the bottom of the board, recent, shaky: 42 only. Nothing else. Please.

Name: NAR_C2_ChapelRegister
title: Chapel Register, Last Page
speaker: Howell Teague, verger
text:
BURIALS, this year, entered late and badly, for which I apologise to God and the diocese.
- Aldous Frey. No body. Company sent a casket and asked us not to open it. We did not open it.
- Ruth Maddern. Same. Same casket maker.
- Ezra Penhallow. Entry struck out and rewritten: NOT DECEASED, REMOVED BY AMBULANCE, SEE CORRESPONDENCE. There is no correspondence.
- Ines Calder. Pulled out of the basin. Nobody sent a casket for her.
NOTE: the crypt lift is condemned. It goes further down than the crypt and I have never liked it.

Name: NAR_C2_SluiceNotice
title: Sluice Gate Operating Notice
speaker: Saltmere Harbor Board
text:
Bolted to the capstan housing, enamel, chipped.
TO CLOSE THE GATE: ship the wheel, then THREE FULL TURNS against the stop. The basin falls about a metre and a half to the mud. Allow four minutes.
TO OPEN: reverse, and stand clear of the chain.
THE WHEEL IS NOT LEFT ON THE CAPSTAN. Children. It lives chained in the bell tower with the ringing gear.
DO NOT CLOSE THE GATE WITH A VESSEL IN THE BASIN. It will sit on the bottom and you will own it.

Name: NAR_C2_FlareLocker
title: Flare Locker Card
speaker: Saltmere Harbor Board
text:
Card wired to the locker handle. The locker is already forced; the hasp is bent back and the seal is torn.
CONTENTS: signal pistol, 25 mm. Cartridges, red, six. For distress use only. Replaced annually.
Six is crossed out. Three is written over it, and under that, in pencil: used three on the thing in the basin and it did not care for them. It went down and stayed down. If you are reading this, it is still in there, and it does not like burning.
No signature.

Name: NAR_C2_HarborChart
title: Chart Table: Mooring Bearings
speaker: Saltmere Harbor Board
text:
A linen chart under glass, pencil bearings taken from the lighthouse lamp room and written in the margin.
BEARINGS FROM THE LAMP (true, not magnetic)
- Chapel spire ............ 040
- Sluice gate housing ..... 115
- Drowned mooring stone ... 250
The stone is the one that only shows at low water, off the west shallows. Three boats on it in my time.
Pencilled under the list: the keeper used these three to true his mirrors every spring. He said the light was only honest if it agreed with the chart.

Name: NAR_C2_HarborLogDrowned
title: Harbor Master's Log, 3 Weeks Back
speaker: Harbor Master J. Vane
text:
0520. Recovered a female body from the basin, west wall, by the capstan housing. Identified as Dr. I. Calder, of Chapel Lane. Coat buttoned, boots laced, torch in her pocket still switched on.
Cause recorded as drowning by the county man, who did not come to the island to record it.
MY OWN NOTE, AND I WILL KEEP IT HERE: the capstan wheel was lying in the mud six feet from her and the chain was cut, not broken. Somebody took that wheel off while she was watching, or she took it off herself and somebody took it back.
I said this twice on the telephone. Nobody wrote it down.

Name: NAR_C2_Footage_Lighthouse
title: Service Camera, Causeway Track
text:
A weatherproof camera on the causeway rail, battery box still warm. The card holds four clips.
CLIP 1, eight months ago, daylight: two men in Vigor coveralls welding a steel plate over the old coal hatch at the lighthouse base.
CLIP 2, same week: a flatbed with crates. The crates go to the lighthouse door. They do not come out.
CLIP 3, three weeks ago, night: a woman in a long coat walking the causeway alone toward the harbor, torch in hand. She does not come back past the camera.
CLIP 4, three days ago: one man, alone, going in with a sample case. The timestamp is the only thing on him that is legible. He does not come back past the camera either.

Name: NAR_C2_KeeperLog
title: Keeper's Bearing Book
speaker: Keeper A. Rell
text:
A hardbacked book chained to the lamp room desk, open at TRUEING THE MIRRORS, SPRING.
The carriage is seized every year by salt. Ship the crank on the lower spindle and work up. ORDER IS ALWAYS LOWER, MIDDLE, UPPER. One, two, three. Never from the top, you will shear the pin.
Set each mirror on its own landmark and the beam gathers on the chart mark by the door, where the brass is worn through.
- LOWER mirror to the chapel spire .... 040
- MIDDLE mirror to the sluice ......... 115
- UPPER mirror to the ................. (the line is scratched out hard, down to the paper. A bearing was written here and somebody removed it.)
The harbor master keeps the same three on his chart table. Go and ask him, it is not a secret, it is a hill and a gate and a stone.

Name: NAR_C2_BrassPlate
title: Brass Plate Under the Lens
speaker: Harlow & Sons, Opticians
text:
HARLOW & SONS - SALTMERE LIGHT - CATADIOPTRIC, 3 PANEL
Each panel runs on its own worm drive. Dials read in 5 degree steps, 000 to 355.
NO HANDLE IS SUPPLIED. The crank is the keeper's property and is to be kept in the lamp room at all times.
Scratched beside the maker's name, much later and much deeper: SERVICE DOOR BEHIND THE CHART. LATCH IS ON THE LIGHT, NOT ON A KEY. THAT WAS NOT MY IDEA.

Name: RAD_C2_Arrival_01
title: Saltmere Landing
speaker: MARA
text: You're on the slipway. I watched your light come across the whole way.

Name: RAD_C2_Arrival_02
title: Saltmere Landing
speaker: LEON
text: Then you've got a better view than I do. Where am I?

Name: RAD_C2_Arrival_03
title: Saltmere Landing
speaker: MARA
text: Quay Row. Chapel Lane is up the hill, the market's at the top of the street, and everything between is under water.

Name: RAD_C2_Arrival_04
title: Saltmere Landing
speaker: LEON
text: And you? That's your window out on the point.

Name: RAD_C2_Arrival_05
title: Saltmere Landing
speaker: MARA
text: Radio station, second floor, door barricaded with a filing cabinet and a dead man's desk. I'm not coming out and you're not coming in.

Name: RAD_C2_Arrival_06
title: Saltmere Landing
speaker: LEON
text: We'll see about the second half of that.

Name: RAD_C2_StreetWarning_01
title: What's In The Water
speaker: MARA
text: Leon. Stop walking. Whatever you just saw take that body, there are more of them and they live in the deep part.

Name: RAD_C2_StreetWarning_02
title: What's In The Water
speaker: LEON
text: They don't come up on the steps?

Name: RAD_C2_StreetWarning_03
title: What's In The Water
speaker: MARA
text: Not if you're quiet. Walk the walls, use the doorways, and get inside a house the second you hear one break surface.

Name: RAD_C2_StreetWarning_04
title: What's In The Water
speaker: LEON
text: Wardrobes and under beds. Like being nine again.

Name: RAD_C2_RadioStation_01
title: The Point
speaker: LEON
text: I'm on the point jetty. Or what's left of it, which is about four metres and a handrail.

Name: RAD_C2_RadioStation_02
title: The Point
speaker: MARA
text: Don't. The shallows between you and me are full of them, I can hear them on the stonework all night.

Name: RAD_C2_RadioStation_03
title: The Point
speaker: LEON
text: I can see your light from here.

Name: RAD_C2_RadioStation_04
title: The Point
speaker: MARA
text: Then look at it and go the other way. I've got water and a door. Find out what did this instead.

Name: RAD_C2_Photo_01
title: The Photograph
speaker: LEON
text: Found a photo in the dead doctor's front room. Ribbon-cutting. Voss from Vigor, shaking hands with a police chief in dress braid.

Name: RAD_C2_Photo_02
title: The Photograph
speaker: MARA
text: Which chief?

Name: RAD_C2_Photo_03
title: The Photograph
speaker: LEON
text: Hale. Marrow Bay. The man whose officers took the container off my team's hands.

Name: RAD_C2_Photo_04
title: The Photograph
speaker: MARA
text: Eleven years of each other's barbecues. That's not a coincidence, that's a friendship.

Name: RAD_C2_Photo_05
title: The Photograph
speaker: LEON
text: It's a friendship with a shipping schedule. Keep it in your head, we'll need it later.

Name: RAD_C2_SafeRoom_01
title: Vestry Check-In
speaker: MARA
text: Relay's strong in there. Thick walls. That's the first clean signal I've had off you since the pier.

Name: RAD_C2_SafeRoom_02
title: Vestry Check-In
speaker: LEON
text: There's a kettle and a locker and nothing trying to kill me. I'll take the ten minutes.

Name: RAD_C2_SafeRoom_03
title: Vestry Check-In
speaker: MARA
text: Check in here whenever you pass. If you stop checking in I'll assume the worst and I'd rather not practise that.

Name: RAD_C2_Diary_01
title: Calder's Pages
speaker: LEON
text: There's a page taped under a desk in the fish market. Dr. Ines Calder, Vigor. She says she split them across three places.

Name: RAD_C2_Diary_02
title: Calder's Pages
speaker: MARA
text: Calder. The harbor master pulled her out of the basin three weeks ago. Everyone said she slipped.

Name: RAD_C2_Diary_03
title: Calder's Pages
speaker: LEON
text: She hid pages in a church, a market and her own cellar. People who slip don't do that.

Name: RAD_C2_Diary_04
title: Calder's Pages
speaker: MARA
text: So what did she find?

Name: RAD_C2_Diary_05
title: Calder's Pages
speaker: LEON
text: That none of this was meant to kill anybody. It was meant to fix people who were already dying. It worked, and this is what working looks like.

Name: RAD_C2_Diary_06
title: Calder's Pages
speaker: MARA
text: That's worse. You understand that's worse.

Name: RAD_C2_HintOrgan_01
title: Hint: The Organ
speaker: MARA
text: That organ's the only thing in the parish that still works. If the doctor hid something, she hid it in the thing nobody would dare touch.

Name: RAD_C2_HintOrgan_02
title: Hint: The Organ
speaker: MARA
text: Ignore the keyboards, they're swollen shut. The verger's note on the bench says pedals only, and the sheet from her cellar is the pedal line.

Name: RAD_C2_HintOrgan_03
title: Hint: The Organ
speaker: MARA
text: Six pedals, left to right as written: D, G, E, D, A, and D again. People drop the last one. Don't.

Name: RAD_C2_MawWarning_01
title: The Thing In The Basin
speaker: MARA
text: Leon, that wake. Get off the low dock, get off it now.

Name: RAD_C2_MawWarning_02
title: The Thing In The Basin
speaker: LEON
text: I've seen it. It's about eleven metres of eel and it's wearing someone's net.

Name: RAD_C2_MawWarning_03
title: The Thing In The Basin
speaker: MARA
text: You can't fight that in water, nobody can. Take the water away from it.

Name: RAD_C2_MawWarning_04
title: The Thing In The Basin
speaker: LEON
text: The gate. Three turns and a metre and a half of mud. Keep talking, I'll be busy.

Name: RAD_C2_HintSluice_01
title: Hint: The Sluice Gate
speaker: MARA
text: Shooting it in deep water is just noise. The basin is the only thing on your side down there, so change it.

Name: RAD_C2_HintSluice_02
title: Hint: The Sluice Gate
speaker: MARA
text: The capstan is on the west wall with the notice bolted to it. Ship the wheel from the bell tower and it's three full turns against the stop.

Name: RAD_C2_HintSluice_03
title: Hint: The Sluice Gate
speaker: MARA
text: One turn per pass, that's all you get. When it beaches, the sac behind the jaw comes open. Put a flare in it.

Name: RAD_C2_HintLens_01
title: Hint: The Lighthouse Lens
speaker: MARA
text: There's no keyhole on that service door, is there. So the lock isn't a lock, it's the light.

Name: RAD_C2_HintLens_02
title: Hint: The Lighthouse Lens
speaker: MARA
text: The keeper's book sets each mirror on a landmark, lower then middle then upper. His third bearing's scratched out, but the harbor master's chart has all three.

Name: RAD_C2_HintLens_03
title: Hint: The Lighthouse Lens
speaker: MARA
text: Lower to the spire, 040. Middle to the sluice, 115. Upper to the drowned mooring stone, 250. In that order or you'll shear the pin.

Name: RAD_C2_StairFound_01
title: Below The Island
speaker: LEON
text: The latch dropped. There's a door behind the keeper's chart and a stone stair going down.

Name: RAD_C2_StairFound_02
title: Below The Island
speaker: MARA
text: Down to what? There's nothing under that rock but rock.

Name: RAD_C2_StairFound_03
title: Below The Island
speaker: LEON
text: Painted steel, cable trays, and air moving up at me. Calder's last page says the work is below the island. She meant it literally.

Name: RAD_C2_StairFound_04
title: Below The Island
speaker: MARA
text: Then I'll lose you on the radio the moment you're under the water line.

Name: RAD_C2_StairFound_05
title: Below The Island
speaker: LEON
text: Keep the set warm and the light on. I'll come up somewhere.

Name: NAR_C3_LockdownNotice
title: Facility Lockdown Notice
speaker: Dr. Elias Voss
text:
EFFECTIVE IMMEDIATELY. Saltmere Annex is closed under clause 14 (containment). All staff out by 18:00. Leave samples in the cold vault. Leave logs where they are.

No incident report will be filed from this site. Questions go to me and to nobody else.

The lift to the crypt stays powered for the salvage crews. Everything else goes dark.

E. Voss

Name: NAR_C3_OrientationCard
title: New Staff Orientation Card
text:
WELCOME TO SALTMERE ANNEX

B1: reception, patient ward, observation, labs, whiteboard bay.
B2: security wing, armory, coolant plant, cooling chamber, cold vault.

B2 is card-controlled. Your card is not a B2 card. Do not ask.

The crypt lift is the only way up to the island. It takes two minutes and it is loud. If you are claustrophobic, say so now, not at minute one.

Name: NAR_C3_VisitorLog
title: Sign-In Sheet (last page)
text:
DATE / NAME / PURPOSE / OUT

14th / R. Imes / damp survey / 11:40
14th / R. Imes / damp survey / 16:02
22nd / salvage crew (3) / cable recovery / 19:15

--- sheet skips four months ---

3 days ago / O. QUINN / sample recovery, cold vault, B2 clearance issued / ----

No out time. The pen is still clipped to the board.

Name: NAR_C3_WardIntake
title: Intake Form: Subject 7
speaker: Dr. Ines Calder
text:
SUBJECT 7. Ezra Penhallow, 68. Fisherman, Saltmere. Referred by the island clinic.

Condition: terminal, four to seven weeks. Weight down 19 kg. Can no longer stand for a full minute.

Consent: given, witnessed, read back to him twice. He asked whether it would hurt. I said I did not know. He said that was honest.

Note for the file: he is not a volunteer of convenience. He is a dying man who was offered strength. I want that written down by someone who was in the room.

I. Calder

Name: NAR_C3_NurseDiary
title: Ward Nurse's Page
speaker: R. Imes
text:
Day eleven with Subject 7.

He calls me girl, which I have decided not to mind. He talks about the boat he sold. He says the worst part of dying was not being able to carry his own gear down the slip.

Today he carried his own water jug to the bed. He laughed about it for a long time. Then he laughed for a bit too long.

Dr. V came down to watch him do it and wrote four lines and left. He did not say one word to Ezra. Not one.

Name: NAR_C3_Footage_Reel1
title: Trial Footage, Reel 1: Intake
text:
Grainy monochrome, ward lighting, timecode 00:00:11.

An old man sits on the edge of a bed in a gown, elbows on his knees, breathing in a way that takes effort. A gloved hand swabs his arm.

EZRA: "Will it be quick, either way?"
CALDER (off camera): "We don't know."
EZRA: "Then put it in before I think about it."

The injection goes in. He watches it go in. The reel ends on him looking at the ceiling, counting under his breath.

Name: NAR_C3_Footage_Reel2
title: Trial Footage, Reel 2: Day Fourteen
text:
Timecode 00:00:03. The same man, standing, no gown now, a vest and trousers that no longer fit.

He lifts a crate of ballast weights that two staff carried in together. He sets it down gently, which is somehow worse.

VOSS (off camera): "Again."

He lifts it again. His forearms are wrong, corded past what skin should hold. At 00:01:48 his head turns to the camera and stays turned for nine seconds without blinking.

VOSS (off camera, quiet): "There. That's the body I wanted."

Name: NAR_C3_Footage_Reel3
title: Trial Footage, Reel 3: Day Fifteen, 04:20
text:
Night lighting. The camera is knocked off level in the first second and films the rest at an angle.

Two staff in the frame. One is trying to talk to him by name. He takes her off her feet without seeming to decide to.

The reel runs forty more seconds. There is no fighting in it after the first eight.

At the end, a door opens. Shoes, not running. Voss steps into frame, looks at the floor, then at the thing standing over it, and speaks to the room.

VOSS: "Log it as a success with a complication. Seal the level. Nobody outside this building hears the word accident."

Name: NAR_C3_OwenRadioLog
title: Handheld Recorder, Last Entry
speaker: Owen Quinn
text:
(breathing, water dripping)

Third day. Cold vault's fine, samples are fine, nothing down here is fine.

I got a B2 card off the chief's board. If anyone reviews this, I took it, it's mine, leave my record alone.

(pause)

Mara. If this ever gets to you. I called the port about the container and they logged it and did nothing, and then I called you instead, and that was me putting it on you. That wasn't fair. You didn't open anything. I did the work that filled it.

Stairwell's flooding and the lift's at the top. I'm going to sit on the landing a while.

Name: NAR_C3_OwenLastNote
title: Folded Note in a Coat Pocket
speaker: Owen Quinn
text:
M —

If I'm late, the tide's in the stair and I'm waiting it out. Don't come down. I mean it this time.

The container is VGR-7718. It is not medical supplies. Whoever signs for it at the port is in it up to the neck.

Tell them it was me who said so, not you. You've got a job and a radio and a town. I've got a badge they can take off me.

— O

Name: NAR_C3_PhotoOwenMara
title: Photograph, Creased in Four
text:
Two people on a slip in summer, squinting. A boy of about nineteen with his arm around his sister's shoulders, both holding one fish between them as if it were a trophy.

On the back, in biro: "you hooked it, I carried it. O."

Name: NAR_C3_MaintNoteConduit
title: Maintenance Snag List
speaker: R. Imes
text:
SNAG 41 — B2 bulkhead reader goes dead maybe twice a week. It is NOT the cards.

The conduit plug in the grey wall box left of the frame works itself loose when the bulkhead slams. Open the box, push the plug home until it clicks twice, then swipe. Works every time.

SNAG 42 — the reader beeps for a good ten seconds while it resets and it carries down the whole corridor. Stand somewhere you can see both ends before you do it.

Name: NAR_C3_TrialLog07
title: V-7 Trial Log, Sheet 07
speaker: Dr. Ines Calder
text:
STRAIN RESPONSE, THERMAL. Ninth repeat, same result.

V-7 holds together at blood warmth and at steady cold. What breaks it is being moved between the two. Call it a cold-shock ladder.

THE LADDER, in order, no stage skipped:
1. Chill the volume to +4 C and HOLD 90 s.
2. Drop to -12 C and HOLD 30 s.
3. Return to +4 C and HOLD 60 s.
4. Purge.

Three stages up and down, then purge. Bonds fail in stage 2 and cannot re-form in stage 3. Skip a stage and it re-forms stronger, so do not improvise.

This is the shape any inhibitor has to be built around. Written here because Dr. Voss will not put it in the main file.

Name: NAR_C3_CalderMemo
title: Re: Re: Subject 7 reclassification
speaker: Dr. Ines Calder
text:
Elias,

You are calling it a therapy in the funding file and a candidate in the lab file and those are two different words.

It took hold in him because he was dying. That is not a feature. That is the only door it can get through, and the moment somebody strong is bitten by somebody who got through that door, the door stops mattering.

I am keeping my own notes. I am not doing it to spite you. I am doing it because in eight months nobody will remember who said what in this corridor.

Ines

Name: NAR_C3_Whiteboard
title: Lab Whiteboard (half wiped)
text:
Written large across the top and not wiped:

   TRIAL 07 / RUN 03 — THERMAL

Under it, a table in the same hand:

   STAGE | TEMP  | HOLD
     1   |  +4 C |  90 s
     2   | -12 C |  30 s
     3   |  +4 C |  60 s
     4   | PURGE |   -

In the corner, boxed and underlined twice:

   CHAMBER INTERLOCK WILL NOT RELEASE THE VAULT UNTIL ALL FOUR STAGES RUN IN ORDER.
   PURGE LAST. PURGE EARLY = RELIEF VENT = START AGAIN.

Name: NAR_C3_ChiefSticky
title: Sticky Note on the Board Frame
text:
To whoever keeps knocking:

I am not coming out to the corridor every time you forget the office code. It is on the board you are standing in front of.

Trial number, then run number. Two digits each, in that order. Four buttons. If you cannot read a board you should not be in my office.

— SEC CHIEF

Name: NAR_C3_SecChiefLog
title: Security Chief's Day Book
text:
Last page, written in three sittings.

Sealed the level like he asked. Counted them out, counted the doors, signed the sheet. Two did not come out and I signed the sheet anyway.

Kept the master key. It is mine until somebody senior enough comes down here to take it off me, which will be never.

Later: head's hot. Bit through my own lip in the night and did not wake up for it. Fuel pack's chafing where the plate sits.

Later: I can hear the pumps through the floor and the pumps are off.

Name: NAR_C3_ShipmentClearance
title: Cold Store Clearance VGR-7718
text:
VIGOR BIOTECH — MOVEMENT CLEARANCE

Consignment: VGR-7718. Origin: Saltmere Annex cold store. Destination: Vigor Tower via Port Halvern Yard C.
Declared contents: medical supplies, refrigerated.
Actual contents, internal line: V-7 stock, live, 14 units.

Cleared for transit, authorised: E. VOSS, Research Director.

Port handling and police escort countersigned:

   W. HALE, Chief of Police, Marrow Bay

Handwritten under the signature: "No customs hold. No manifest copy to the harbour office."

Name: NAR_C3_VossMemoSeal
title: Annex closure, final
speaker: Dr. Elias Voss
text:
To site security, copy to nobody.

The two staff we lost are recorded as a plant-room accident. That is the only version. If a family asks, they ask the company, not you.

Subject 7 remains on the level. He is not a disposal problem, he is data. Keep the ward doors shut and the power on the lift.

We move the programme to the tower. Eight months and a better room and this becomes the thing I said it was.

E.V.

Name: NAR_C3_ArmoryInventory
title: Armory Board
text:
RACK CHECK — signed weekly, last signature eight months old.

1. Bolt rifle ............ PRESENT
2. Bolt rifle ............ SIGNED OUT, SEC CHIEF, not returned
3. Shot ................. transferred to Yard C escort
4. Flare pistol ......... transferred to harbour master, Saltmere

Rifle rounds: two boxes. Count them in and out. I will know.

Name: NAR_C3_SumpWarning
title: Taped to the Stair Door, B2
speaker: R. Imes
text:
PUMPS ARE OFF. Lower level is holding about a metre and rising a hand's width a week.

Do not wade it in boots you care about and do not wade it alone.

And before anyone laughs at me again: something took the float switch off its chain. The chain is bitten. I have kept it in my locker.

Name: NAR_C3_ValveProcedure
title: Cooling Chamber Operating Card
text:
Laminated, chained to the valve gallery rail.

VALVE 1 — BRINE INTAKE. Floods the chamber and pulls it down to +4 C.
VALVE 2 — CRYO. Takes a flooded chamber to -12 C. Will not bite on a dry chamber.
VALVE 3 — PURGE. Dumps the chamber to the sump and ends the run.

GAUGE above the gallery shows chamber temperature. A green HOLD lamp lights when the stage temperature is reached and goes out when the hold time is served.

Work the valves one at a time. Serve every hold. If the sequence is wrong the relief vent blows live steam across the gallery and the run resets.

Name: NAR_C3_ColdVaultManifest
title: Cold Vault Carousel Card
speaker: Dr. Ines Calder
text:
CAROUSEL 2, POSITION 1 — "A". Inhibitor base, cold-set. Stable at vault temperature, stable in a hand for a few hours, dead if it warms past that.

A on its own does nothing at all. It is one third of a thing.

B (binder) and C (carrier) were never made here. They are at the tower, and so is the only machine that will put the three of them together, and that machine wants the thermal ladder from sheet 07 or it spits the batch out.

Whoever is reading this: take all three or take none.

Name: RAD_C3_Descent_01
title: Into the tunnel
speaker: MARA
text: You're under the island now. I can hear the rock in your mic.

Name: RAD_C3_Descent_02
title: Into the tunnel
speaker: LEON
text: There's a bulkhead ahead with a company serial on it. Your island has a basement.

Name: RAD_C3_Descent_03
title: Into the tunnel
speaker: MARA
text: Nobody ever said a word about anything under the lighthouse.

Name: RAD_C3_Descent_04
title: Into the tunnel
speaker: LEON
text: That's usually the point of a basement. Stay on this channel.

Name: RAD_C3_Reception_01
title: Reception
speaker: LEON
text: Reception, lights on half, closure notice on the desk. Signed by a Doctor Voss.

Name: RAD_C3_Reception_02
title: Reception
speaker: MARA
text: Is there a sign-in sheet? Tell me if there's a sign-in sheet.

Name: RAD_C3_Reception_03
title: Reception
speaker: LEON
text: There is. Why does that matter to you right now?

Name: RAD_C3_Reception_04
title: Reception
speaker: MARA
text: (a long pause, then a metal sound at her end) There's a lift in the church crypt. I'm in it.

Name: RAD_C3_Reception_05
title: Reception
speaker: LEON
text: Mara, go back up.

Name: RAD_C3_Reception_06
title: Reception
speaker: MARA
text: It only goes one way once it starts. Two minutes.

Name: RAD_C3_FootageTalk_01
title: After the third reel
speaker: LEON
text: Found their trial footage. A man named Penhallow. He was dying and he said yes.

Name: RAD_C3_FootageTalk_02
title: After the third reel
speaker: MARA
text: Ezra? He sold his boat to my neighbour. We thought he died in a hospice.

Name: RAD_C3_FootageTalk_03
title: After the third reel
speaker: LEON
text: He didn't. And the man running it stood in the room afterwards and called it a success.

Name: RAD_C3_FootageTalk_04
title: After the third reel
speaker: MARA
text: (static, her breathing) Lift's slowing. I'm nearly down.

Name: DLG_C3_OwenTruth_01
title: The stairwell
speaker: LEON
text: Technician. Vigor jacket. He's got a B2 card in his hand.

Name: DLG_C3_OwenTruth_02
title: The stairwell
speaker: MARA
text: Don't move him.

Name: DLG_C3_OwenTruth_03
title: The stairwell
speaker: LEON
text: You know him.

Name: DLG_C3_OwenTruth_04
title: The stairwell
speaker: MARA
text: Owen. He's my brother. He worked for them.

Name: DLG_C3_OwenTruth_05
title: The stairwell
speaker: MARA
text: He called me three days ago. He said a container was coming through the port and nobody should open it.

Name: DLG_C3_OwenTruth_06
title: The stairwell
speaker: LEON
text: And you had a radio.

Name: DLG_C3_OwenTruth_07
title: The stairwell
speaker: MARA
text: I had the whole port on a radio. I said nothing, because saying it meant saying his name.

Name: DLG_C3_OwenTruth_08
title: The stairwell
speaker: MARA
text: Two nights later they opened it anyway. So it didn't even buy him anything.

Name: DLG_C3_OwenTruth_09
title: The stairwell
speaker: LEON
text: (after a moment) I've seen what one phone call to the right desk does. Usually nothing.

Name: DLG_C3_OwenTruth_10
title: The stairwell
speaker: MARA
text: That's not absolution.

Name: DLG_C3_OwenTruth_11
title: The stairwell
speaker: LEON
text: No. It's a fact. Take the photo out of his pocket, leave him the coat. We need the card.

Name: RAD_C3_HintKeycard_01
title: Hint: B2 bulkhead
speaker: MARA
text: The card's good, I watched it light the panel orange. So it isn't the card.

Name: RAD_C3_HintKeycard_02
title: Hint: B2 bulkhead
speaker: MARA
text: There's a snag list back in the labs that moans about this exact reader. Grey wall box, left of the frame.

Name: RAD_C3_HintKeycard_03
title: Hint: B2 bulkhead
speaker: MARA
text: Open the box, push the loose plug in until it clicks twice, then swipe. And watch the corridor, the reset beeps for ages.

Name: RAD_C3_HintWhiteboard_01
title: Hint: security office code
speaker: MARA
text: Four digits and a note from a man who thought he was being funny. It's on the board.

Name: RAD_C3_HintWhiteboard_02
title: Hint: security office code
speaker: MARA
text: Read the top line of the whiteboard, not the table. Trial number, then run number.

Name: RAD_C3_HintWhiteboard_03
title: Hint: security office code
speaker: MARA
text: Trial seven, run three. Two digits each. Zero seven, zero three.

Name: RAD_C3_HintValves_01
title: Hint: cooling chamber
speaker: MARA
text: The vault's holding its own door shut. It wants the chamber run properly first.

Name: RAD_C3_HintValves_02
title: Hint: cooling chamber
speaker: MARA
text: That log you copied down. Four stages, plus four, minus twelve, plus four, purge. The gauge is the board, the valves are the pen.

Name: RAD_C3_HintValves_03
title: Hint: cooling chamber
speaker: MARA
text: Intake until the lamp dies, cryo until it dies, shut cryo and intake again until it dies, then purge. Purge last or the vent blows.

Name: DLG_C3_FirstBrute_01
title: The thing in the wing
speaker: MARA
text: That one's wearing armour.

Name: DLG_C3_FirstBrute_02
title: The thing in the wing
speaker: LEON
text: It was wearing it before. Body's grown into the plate.

Name: DLG_C3_FirstBrute_03
title: The thing in the wing
speaker: LEON
text: Don't trade shots with it. Doors and corners.

Name: DLG_C3_ColdVault_01
title: Cold vault
speaker: LEON
text: Component A. Calder's writing says it's a third of a cure.

Name: DLG_C3_ColdVault_02
title: Cold vault
speaker: MARA
text: A third is more than this island's had all night.

Name: DLG_C3_ColdVault_03
title: Cold vault
speaker: LEON
text: The other two are in their tower in the city. With the machine that mixes them.

Name: DLG_C3_ColdVault_04
title: Cold vault
speaker: MARA
text: Then we're going to the city. Say it like it's a plan and I'll believe it.

Name: RAD_C3_HintWarden_01
title: Hint: the Warden
speaker: MARA
text: Pistol's doing nothing to that plate. Use the room.

Name: RAD_C3_HintWarden_02
title: Hint: the Warden
speaker: MARA
text: Yellow gas valves on the bay walls. Open one, get him standing in it, then drop the blast door on the bay.

Name: RAD_C3_HintWarden_03
title: Hint: the Warden
speaker: MARA
text: The blast strips his back plate. There's a fuel line under it. Shoot the line while it's bare, you've got about four seconds.

Name: DLG_C3_WardenAfter_01
title: After the Warden
speaker: MARA
text: He had the keys to every door down here and he still couldn't leave.

Name: DLG_C3_WardenAfter_02
title: After the Warden
speaker: LEON
text: He sealed two people in and signed the sheet. Then he stayed with it.

Name: DLG_C3_WardenAfter_03
title: After the Warden
speaker: MARA
text: The far wall's down. There's salt air coming through it.

Name: DLG_C3_SeaCave_01
title: Sea cave
speaker: LEON
text: Maintenance raft. Oars, a bailing can, and about a foot of freeboard.

Name: DLG_C3_SeaCave_02
title: Sea cave
speaker: MARA
text: I row. You've got the gun and I've got twenty years of this water.

Name: DLG_C3_SeaCave_03
title: Sea cave
speaker: LEON
text: Then I'll call it. Left and right, loud, and you don't argue.

Name: DLG_C3_SeaCave_04
title: Sea cave
speaker: MARA
text: Mainland's that way. Four miles of nothing to hide behind.

Name: RAD_C3_HintUndertow_01
title: Hint: the Undertow
speaker: MARA
text: I can't steer and watch. Call it or we're on the rocks.

Name: RAD_C3_HintUndertow_02
title: Hint: the Undertow
speaker: MARA
text: It opens that eye before it swings. That's your window, not after.

Name: RAD_C3_HintUndertow_03
title: Hint: the Undertow
speaker: MARA
text: If it's got hold of the raft, shoot the arm, not the eye. Free us first.

Name: DLG_C3_Shore_01
title: The mainland shore
speaker: MARA
text: Marrow Bay. Half those streets should be lit.

Name: DLG_C3_Shore_02
title: The mainland shore
speaker: LEON
text: Count the sirens instead. They stopped moving an hour ago.

Name: DLG_C3_Shore_03
title: The mainland shore
speaker: MARA
text: Who do we hand that clearance sheet to? Because one of the names on it runs the police.

Name: DLG_C3_Shore_04
title: The mainland shore
speaker: LEON
text: Then we start with him. Pull the raft up past the tide line, we're not coming back for it.

Name: NAR_C4_EvacNotice
title: Emergency Notice: Zones 3 and 4
speaker: Marrow Bay City Office
text:
ZONES 3 AND 4 ARE UNDER EVACUATION ORDER.
Coaches leave Harbour Avenue every twenty minutes until 03:00. Carry nothing larger than one bag.

Do not drink from taps in Zones 3, 4 or 5 until the water office clears them.

If a member of your household is unwell, elderly, or cannot walk to the coach, do NOT wait with them. Mark the door with tape and report the address at the plaza checkpoint.

This notice is issued on the authority of Chief W. Hale, Marrow Bay Police.

Name: NAR_C4_CarNote
title: Note under a wiper blade
speaker: Dinah
text:
Rob - if you get back to the car before me, we went on foot. The avenue is solid, nobody is moving. I have Ellie and your mother.

They would not let your mother on the coach. The officer said she'd slow the aisle. I'm not leaving her in the flat with tape on the door, I don't care what the notice says.

We are going up to the plaza. If the plaza is shut we are going to the station, there are police there at least.

Don't wait at the car. Please.

Name: NAR_C4_RuizLetter
title: Unsent letter in a jacket pocket
speaker: Ana Ruiz
text:
Cris - I'm writing this in the ambulance bay because I can't say it on the phone.

Something happened at the port the night before last and we were told not to write it up. Not told. Ordered, in person, by the chief, to eleven of us in a room with the door shut.

I did write it up. It's in the archive where it belongs and I kept the key on me, which is probably stupid of me.

If I'm slow coming home this week that's why. Feed the cat.

Name: NAR_C4_RuizCamA
title: Body camera 4471, clip A: Yard C, 17:38
speaker: Ana Ruiz
text:
Night rain, floodlights, the side of a container with VGR-7718 stencilled on it. Six officers in port police jackets, none of them port police.

Three federal agents are kneeling on the wet concrete with their hands flat on their heads. The tall one keeps talking.

PRUITT (off camera): "Agent Dale Pruitt. Federal. That container is evidence, Chief."
HALE: "Then it's police evidence now."
PRUITT: "You don't have the authority and you know it."
HALE: "Put him in a van."

A younger agent moves and someone fires twice. The camera jerks to the ground, then up. The tall one is walking to the van with an officer's hand on his neck. Hale is holding his own forearm and looking at it.

RUIZ (close, quiet): "Four-four-seven-one, I'm still recording."

Name: NAR_C4_RuizCamB
title: Body camera 4471, clip B: station lobby, 01:12
speaker: Ana Ruiz
text:
The watch desk. Ruiz's hand comes into frame and hangs a key on the duty board, then takes it back off again.

RUIZ: "Logging it out properly. Evidence room, one key, Ruiz."
DESK OFFICER: "You're not supposed to have that."
RUIZ: "Then write that down too."

She walks into the archive. The camera swings across rolling stacks and stops on a records cabinet with brass letter plates. Her hand pulls out her own drawer, drops the key inside, and slides it shut.

RUIZ: "My drawer, my mess."

The clip ends in the corridor. Somebody is screaming two floors down.

Name: NAR_C4_DutyLog
title: Watch desk duty log, night shift
text:
KEYS OUT / KEYS IN - NIGHT SHIFT

22:40 Garage 2 - Okonjo - returned 23:55
23:15 Cell block - Dolan - NOT RETURNED
00:20 Armoury cage - Hale - NOT RETURNED
01:12 Evidence room - Ruiz - NOT RETURNED (see note)
01:30 Archive - Ruiz - returned 01:41

Note added by desk: Ruiz was told twice she is not on the evidence list this month. She logged it anyway. Taking it up with the sergeant when the sergeant exists again.

02:05 Everything after this is on the floor somewhere, we stopped writing.

Name: NAR_C4_ArchiveIndex
title: Records cabinet index card
text:
PERSONAL RECORDS CABINET - HOW IT WORKS

One drawer per serving officer, filed by surname letter, A at the top left to Z at the bottom right. Shared letters share a drawer.

Your drawer is for your own notebooks, court diaries and personal property while on shift. It is NOT an evidence store. It is NOT a key store. We have a duty board for keys.

Drawers do not lock. That is deliberate. If you need something locked, ask the custody sergeant.

- Records clerk

Name: NAR_C4_CellBlockLog
title: Custody log, page torn at the corner
text:
CELL 1 - empty
CELL 2 - male, no name given, no charge entered. Brought in 18:40 with the other one. Deceased 19:05. Doctor not called.
CELL 3 - empty
CELL 4 - male, no name given, no charge entered. Brought in 18:40. Injury to left forearm, dressed by officers, medic refused.

Across the bottom in a different hand: NO RECORD. CHIEF'S ORDERS. DO NOT ENTER THESE TWO IN THE SYSTEM.

Under that, in pencil: I am entering them in this book because this book is not the system.

Name: NAR_C4_EvidenceIntake
title: Evidence intake sheet, locker 17
speaker: Custody Sgt. Okonjo
text:
LOCKER 17 - COURT SEAL

Contents: one bound ledger, hard cover, handwritten. Seized from a vehicle on Harbour Avenue, 11 Sep. Marked V.B. PAYMENTS on the spine.

Sealed on the application of CID. Under seal this locker cannot be opened from the cell block or from here. The bolt releases from the CID desk terminal and only from there, with an authorised print.

Do not cut the bolt. Do not ask me to cut the bolt. Det. Sgt. Ferris has been very clear that this one goes to court in one piece.

Name: NAR_C4_FerrisBookingCard
title: Booking print cards, sleeve of three
text:
Three grey cards in one plastic sleeve, each with ten inked boxes and a classification line at the top.

CARD 1 - MARSH, D. - booked 02 Aug, affray - RIGHT INDEX: LOOP - ridge count 9
CARD 2 - FERRIS, M., Det. Sgt. - booked 14 Sep, complaint withdrawn same day - RIGHT INDEX: WHORL - ridge count 14
CARD 3 - UNKNOWN MALE - booked 18:40 last night, no charge entered - RIGHT INDEX: ARCH - ridge count 11

On the back of card 2, in biro: "Booked by his own chief on a Monday and back at his desk by Tuesday. Whole thing was a message."

Name: NAR_C4_PruittTape
title: Confiscated recorder, property bag 7-C
speaker: Dale Pruitt
text:
Pruitt, continuing. Whoever finds this, the tape is the report.

We landed at the port at thirteen hundred. The container was already open and already wrong. Cold mist still coming off the floor of it at eleven hours.

The port police turned up with the chief of a city force that has no business at a port. They took Ortiz's camera and they took the manifests.

I got my hand on the chief's arm and he pulled away like I'd burned him. He had a dressing under the sleeve. He has been bitten and he is walking around giving orders.

If you are federal, go up. Not out. Up.

Name: NAR_C4_FerrisMemo
title: Re: V.B. ledger - please read before Friday
speaker: Det. Sgt. M. Ferris
text:
To: K. Abiola, County Prosecutor's Office
From: M. Ferris, Marrow Bay CID

Kemi - the book is real and it is in my evidence room under seal, locker 17.

Six transfers over seven months from a Vigor Biotech holding account to an account in the chief's wife's maiden name. Two of the six came back the same week, I assume because somebody at their end got nervous. Four of them cleared and stayed cleared.

I want the four, not the six. The four are the case.

He had me booked and printed last month on a complaint that evaporated by lunchtime. I know what that was. Please move fast.

Name: NAR_C4_PrintLockManual
title: PrintLock 2 quick guide, taped to the monitor
text:
CID DESK TERMINAL - SEAL RELEASE

1. Wake the pad. The screen shows the last print this terminal accepted, as a classification and a ridge count. That is the print the seal is registered to.
2. Lay the booking card face down on the glass, square to the arrows. The pad reads the inked right index box.
3. Match on classification AND ridge count. A wrong card is not a free guess: three wrong reads lock the pad for ninety seconds and sound the desk alarm.
4. On a match the terminal releases the bolt on the named locker. Go and open it by hand. The terminal does not open anything up here.
